Core concept

An atom is the simplest unit of an element

Cut a substance into smaller and smaller pieces and you reach a particle that cannot be cut any further.

Learn
  • Wood is made up of different substances. The most abundant compound found in wood is cellulose.Wood is not one single thing. It is several substances mixed together. The one there is most of is called cellulose, and it is the part that gives wood its stiffness.
  • Cellulose is made up of the elements carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, which are chemically combined.Three different elements are joined together to build cellulose. Joined chemically means they are locked together, not just sitting side by side like sand and salt in a jar.
  • Each of these elements consists of atoms. An atom is the simplest unit of an element.Take carbon and keep cutting. You end up with one carbon atom. You cannot cut that in half and still have carbon, so the atom is where the element stops.
  • The word atom comes from the Greek word atomos, which means cannot be cut or indivisible.The people who named it thought the atom could never be split. The name stuck, even though we now know an atom does have smaller parts inside it.
  • Each element in the periodic table consists of only one type of atom. The element carbon consists of only carbon atoms.One element, one kind of atom. That is what makes gold gold and carbon carbon.
Key Facts
  • An atom is the simplest unit of an element.
  • Each element consists of only one type of atom.
  • Cellulose is a compound: its carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms are chemically combined, not merely mixed.
Test

Which statement describes an atom?

Core concept

How small is an atom?

An atom cannot be seen with the naked eye, so we describe its size by comparing it with objects we can see.

Learn
  • An atom cannot be seen with the naked eye.No matter how hard you look, and no matter how good the school microscope is, you will never see one atom. They are far below what light can show us.
  • A row of 1 million carbon atoms can take up the diameter of a strand of human hair that is between 0.001 cm and 0.006 cm.Pull out one hair and look at its width. You would have to lay a million carbon atoms side by side to reach across it.
  • A row of 50 million hydrogen atoms can take up the length of a grain of rice that is about 0.5 cm.
  • A row of over 100 million hydrogen atoms can take up the length of a fingernail that is about 1 cm.One centimetre sounds small until you realise it takes more than a hundred million hydrogen atoms in a line to cover it.
  • One of the largest atoms we know of is the caesium atom, and even a caesium atom is only about 0.000000007 cm across.Even the big ones are tiny. That number has eight zeros after the decimal point before the seven appears.
Key Facts
  • Atoms are far too small to be seen with the naked eye.
  • Different atoms have different sizes. The caesium atom is one of the largest we know of, at about 0.000000007 cm.

Core concept

What is a nanoscale object?

Nanoscale objects are smaller than one billionth of a metre, and new instruments are what let scientists study them.

Stepping down to the nanoscale4 steps
1Tap each step to zoom in. Watch how far you have to go before you reach a single atom.
Tap Fingernail to begin.
Learn
  • Nanoscale objects are tiny objects with sizes of less than 0.000000001 metre, or one billionth of a metre.Split one metre into a thousand million equal pieces. One of those pieces is the size we are talking about.
  • An example is DNA, which is found in cells in the human body. A strand of human DNA is about 0.0000000025 m in diameter.
  • Scientists use special instruments to observe nanoscale objects, such as the atomic force microscope and the scanning tunnelling microscope.An ordinary microscope uses light, and light is simply too coarse for something this small. These instruments feel the surface instead of looking at it.
  • Nanotechnology is the field of science that involves nanoscale objects and their applications.It is a whole area of science built on working with things at that size, and on what you can build once you can.
  • Applications include using very small robots, known as nanorobots, to deliver drugs into the bloodstream and to repair damaged cells.The idea is that a machine small enough to travel in your blood could carry medicine to exactly the place that needs it, instead of dosing the whole body.
Key Facts
  • Nanoscale means a size of less than 0.000000001 m, which is one billionth of a metre.
  • Nanotechnology is the field of science that involves nanoscale objects and their applications.
  • Technological advances are what allowed scientists to find evidence about what matter is made of.
Test

Why can an ordinary school microscope not show a nanoscale object?

Core concept

What is inside an atom?

An atom contains three types of sub-atomic particle, and each one has its own charge and its own place.

Learn
  • An atom contains three types of sub-atomic particles, namely the proton, the neutron and the electron.Sub-atomic simply means smaller than an atom. The atom turned out not to be the end of the story after all.
  • A proton is a positively charged particle.
  • A neutron is a particle with no charge.
  • An electron is a negatively charged particle. It moves around the nucleus at high speed.Electrons never sit still. They race around the outside of the atom, which is why we draw them on paths rather than as fixed dots.
  • Protons and neutrons form the nucleus of an atom, while electrons move around the nucleus.Everything heavy is packed into a tiny lump at the centre. Everything light is out at the edges, moving.
  • The nucleus is made up of neutrons and protons. Thus, it is positively charged.Protons are positive and neutrons are neutral, so adding them together leaves the whole centre positive.
Key Facts
  • The nucleus is made up of neutrons and protons. Thus, it is positively charged.
  • Protons and neutrons stay within the nucleus. Electrons move around the nucleus.
  • No one knows what an atom looks like exactly. The planetary model is only a simplified representation of the atomic structure.

Why do we say an atom is mostly empty space?

The nucleus holds almost all the mass but takes up almost none of the room, so almost anything fired at an atom goes straight through.

History of science

How has our model of the atom changed?

Each model was the best picture available at the time, and each was replaced when it could no longer explain what was measured.

Three pictures of one atomPanel 1 / 5
1Press Next panel to follow how the picture of the atom changed.
Press Next panel.
Learn
  • No one knows what an atom looks like exactly.Nobody has ever seen one, so every picture of an atom is a picture somebody built to make the science easier to think about.
  • The planetary model is only a simplified representation of the atomic structure, used to allow for the scientific study of atoms.It is a working picture, not a photograph. It is good enough for what we need in this chapter and wrong in ways that matter to a physicist.
  • Scientific models like the planetary model help us to represent and study natural phenomena.A model is a thinking tool. If it helps you predict and explain, it is doing its job, even if it is not a true likeness.
  • Older models are replaced when they cannot explain what is measured, which is why science stays reliable.Being replaced is not a failure. A model that survives every new measurement is either very good or is not being tested hard enough.
Key Facts
  • No one knows what an atom looks like exactly.
  • Models are simplified representations. They are judged by what they can explain, not by how real they look.
  • As new evidence is found, what is accepted by scientists today may be changed or replaced in the future.
Test

Why are the billiard ball model and the plum pudding model no longer used?

Core concept

Why is an atom electrically neutral?

The number of protons is equal to the number of electrons, so the positive and negative charges cancel out.

Learn
  • In an atom, the number of protons is equal to the number of electrons.Count the positives and count the negatives in any atom and you get the same answer both times.
  • Thus, the positive and negative charges in the atom are balanced. The atom is said to be electrically neutral.Every plus has a minus to cancel it, so from the outside the atom behaves as though it had no charge at all.
  • Neutrons do not contribute to the overall charge of an atom as they do not have any charges.Neutrons are along for the ride as far as charge goes. Change how many there are and the overall charge still comes out as zero.
  • A proton has a relative charge of +1, a neutron has a relative charge of 0, and an electron has a relative charge of −1.
  • A proton and a neutron each have a relative mass of 1, while an electron has a relative mass of 1/1840.An electron weighs almost nothing next to a proton. It would take more than eighteen hundred of them to match a single one.
  • The mass of an atom is mainly contributed by the mass of its nucleus, so the mass of the electrons is considered negligible.Almost all the mass is in that tiny central lump. The electrons add so little that we ignore them when working out the mass.
Key Facts
  • The atom is electrically neutral because the number of protons is equal to the number of electrons.
  • Neutrons do not contribute to the overall charge of an atom as they do not have any charges.
  • The mass of an atom is mainly contributed by the mass of its nucleus.
Test

An atom has 8 protons. What else must be true?

Core concept

Why can two atoms of the same element have different masses?

The number of neutrons in an atom is not always equal to the number of protons, and it can differ between atoms of the same element.

Learn
  • Unlike the number of electrons, the number of neutrons in an atom is not always equal to the number of protons in the atom.Protons and electrons always match. Neutrons do not have to match anything, so their number is free to vary.
  • A carbon atom has 6 protons and 6 electrons, but it may have 6, 7 or 8 neutrons.All three are still carbon, because carbon is decided by the protons. The extra neutrons only make the atom heavier.
  • A nitrogen atom has 7 protons and 7 electrons, and it may have 7 or 8 neutrons.
  • A uranium atom has 92 protons and 92 electrons, and it may have 143 or 146 neutrons.
  • Some elements have atoms with different numbers of neutrons. These atoms are known as isotopes.Same element, same chemistry, different weight. Isotopes are the name for that family of near twins.
  • Nitrogen-14 and nitrogen-15 are both isotopes of the element nitrogen, while uranium-235 and uranium-238 are isotopes of the element uranium.The number written after the name counts the protons and neutrons together, which is why the heavier twin has the bigger number.
Key Facts
  • The number of protons never changes for a given element. The number of neutrons can.
  • Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are known as isotopes.
  • Because the mass of an atom comes mainly from its nucleus, isotopes of one element have different masses.

Inside the nucleus

  • Protons: relative charge +1, relative mass 1

Around the nucleus
